newsitem.title: USA: Florida judge refuses rehearing in Bucs bonds case.
newsitem.headline: Florida judge refuses rehearing in Bucs bonds case.

text.p: A Florida judge declined Wednesday to rehear a validation request for $204.5 million of revenue bonds to finance the Tampa Bay Buccaneers' new stadium.
But Circuit Judge Sam Pendino urged Hillsborough County and the football team to revise the stadium lease contract that contained a provision he found objectionable.

"I do not believe I have the authority to rewrite this contract," Pendino said. "I'm asking you and the Bucs to make a good faith effort to work this out. If you do, let me know and I will validate the bond issue because the Bucs provide the community with a substantial benefit."

Pendino refused Friday to validate the tax-exempt revenue bond issue by the Tampa Sports Authority. He said a lease provision giving the team the first $2 million of annual revenues from non-Bucs events at the stadium made the project one primarily for private gain, and that it would be unconstitutional to use tax-backed bonds for that purpose.

County Attorney Emeline Acton sought a rehearing Wednesday. She said "severability" language in the lease contract with the team specifies that if one part of the deal is deemed unconstitutional, the rest would be unaffected.
She said that although the judge objected to the $2 million annual payment, the rest of the contract, which uses sales taxes to pay debt service on the bonds, would remain valid.
The judge said he could not strike the lease provision without hearing from Bucs' representatives, who did not attend the brief hearing Wednesday afternoon.
But Pendino said he would reconsider the validation if the county and the team revised the contract on their own.
Acton said she did not know whether the county would pursue that option or appeal to the Florida Supreme Court.
Hillsborough County voters approved a sales tax increase in September to finance school and public safety projects and the stadium. The bonds were to have been issued in October.

Former Tampa Mayor Bill Poe sued the county, city of Tampa and Tampa Sports Authority to block the bond issue on grounds that it would mainly benefit the privately owned team. The lawsuit was later merged with the bond validation process.
